# Yang--Mills research workflow

For work on four-dimensional pure Yang--Mills existence or the mass gap, use
`$ym-run-clay-program` as the orchestrator and finish every research phase with
`$ym-audit-frontier`.

When dependent bad-set moments must be converted into a full-measure block
process, use `$ym-prove-adaptive-block-domination`. Require a history-uniform
conditional bound; intersection moments alone are not a domination theorem.

When rare retained boundary states can force later defects, use
`$ym-prove-state-weighted-defect-transfer`. Require a positive physical weight,
a uniform root moment, and `QV<=qV`; do not erase entry cost by taking an
unnecessary scalar supremum over microscopic histories.

When a local action or large-field charge must become a normalized conditional
probability, use `$ym-prove-conditional-partition-ratio`. Retain the good and
bad partition functions, transition-state weight, entropy, and the supremum
over positive-mass boundary states.

If the repository starts from the July 2026 package frontier, do not repeat the
one-link denominator, canonical witness, or single-star repair searches. The
exact nonlinear dispersion geometry and normalized transfer theorem close the
continuous channel in the centered retained reference at
`7.757562504510382e-5`, but boundary-uniform physical transfer is open. The
generic single-star link repair is independently falsified by its exact
spillover spectrum. Use `$ym-prove-conditional-partition-ratio`,
`$ym-prove-adaptive-block-domination`,
`$ym-prove-state-weighted-defect-transfer`, and
`$ym-control-large-fields-and-topology` to prove, uniformly over every finite
volume and positive-mass retained history `h`,
`mu_h(A intersect G_h) <= exp(ell_h) nu_h(A intersect G_h)` and
`mu_h(G_h^c) <= q_exc,h`, with
`q_low,h + exp(ell_h)q_gauss,h + q_exc,h <= 0.0009721110007367992`.
Keep center-sector ratios, cut/orbit control, and nonabelian integer topology
as separate owned channels; do not infer integer topology from center labels.

Maintain the following implication chain as separate proof obligations:

1. regulated gauge-invariant construction;
2. controlled, gauge-covariant RG trajectory;
3. entry into an independently defined infrared rigidity basin;
4. uniform physical correlation rigidity;
5. coherent continuum Schwinger data with the required positivity and locality;
6. Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction;
7. a positive Hamiltonian spectral gap above a unique vacuum.

For every result, label its status as one of: exact theorem, conditional theorem,
finite-dimensional certificate, numerical calibration, falsification, conjecture,
or open frontier. Never promote a finite-volume lattice gap, standalone plaquette
tail, perturbative beta function, incomplete observable sector, or assumed
clustering estimate to a continuum mass gap.

Preserve gauge invariance, locality, reflection positivity, observable
completeness, physical scale normalization, and uniform cutoff/volume quantifiers
whenever a representation or limit changes. Record explicitly what each map
forgets and which certificates it transports.

Each phase should produce:

- a frozen theorem or obstruction statement with all quantifiers;
- a dependency graph and frontier ledger;
- adversarial calibration against restricted models or boundary conditions;
- executable finite certificates and tests where possible;
- a concise next-target decision based on the first unproved implication.

Do not base new work on an earlier regulator or Wilson-action calculation unless
it is necessary for a stated comparison, universality bridge, or calibration.

For publication work, choose exactly one candidate and use its dedicated skill:
`$ym-draft-frustration-obstruction`, `$ym-draft-finite-block-certificate`,
`$ym-draft-representational-dynamics`, or
`$ym-draft-heat-kernel-enclosures`.  Keep each manuscript self-contained,
remove stage narration, distinguish proof from computation, perform a primary
literature audit, and finish with `$ym-audit-frontier`.

Within that paper-specific workflow, use `$ym-develop-paper-proofs` to freeze
and close the theorem, `$ym-ground-paper-literature` to build claim-level
grounding, `$ym-frame-paper-narrative` for motivation and introduction,
`$ym-build-proof-appendix` for complete deferred details, and
`$ym-build-latex-paper` to lint, compile, render, and verify the final PDF.
